claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI and custom-silicon businesses each passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
Gartner says by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says cloud value from innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings and EBITDA uplift of 20-30% by 2030 for high-performing organizations.
McKinsey's report says Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and chips business (including Trainium and Graviton) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, with Azure revenue growing 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195-205 billion, up from an earlier $180-190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations of $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year.
Oracle's AI infrastructure contracts include prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
ResearchAndMarkets says hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310-330B by 2030.
Mordor Intelligence says 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi's 2026 survey covered 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Gartner predicts by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.

Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney that AI doesn't deliver value on its own and needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance.
Gartner says by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said developers are standardizing on CNCF projects and organizations are extending those platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, and human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 82% agree AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes while manual approval remains close to universal, which Pulumi's report describes as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's survey, teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence says the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, and 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to growing maturity.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects.
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server enabling infrastructure access for AI assistants.
Pulumi integrates with CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
The 2026 edition's predictions held up.
